decisions.reason: The question asks whether token-level highlighting helps users identify what to edit. It omits the explicit comparison between highlighting likely edits and highlighting low-probability tokens.
The method describes what the edit model predicts but omits the preliminary data from nine coders who corrected Codex outputs until the tasks were completed properly.

The poster gives the sample size and the number and difficulty of the tasks. It omits the participants’ employment at a large US technology company, their Python experience, and randomization of task order and tool-to-task assignments.
The method identifies Davinci-002 Codex, all three presentation conditions, and both thresholds. It omits that the thresholds were chosen to match total highlight counts across the three tasks.

The result gives all three mean times with the correct conditions and distinguishes the significant advantage over Generation probability from the comparison with Prediction only. The caption gives the 10-minute cap.

Panel (b) visually shows the expected survival pattern. The poster leaves the exact rates to be estimated from the bars, does not define survival as a token remaining untouched, and does not explain how the pattern indicates more localized editing.
Panel (c) shows higher preference for Edit model highlights and a scale ending at 7. The poster omits the exact means, p-value, item topics, and reverse-coding of distraction.
The poster omits that the edit model was trained on the same completions evaluated in the study and that comparable effects on unseen tasks remain unverified.
The poster omits that more accurate human oversight and reduced automation bias remain untested.

notes: The title and section headings are easy to scan. The three figure panels have small axis labels, condition names, and legend text that are difficult to read at the supplied size. The question-to-method sequence is clear, though the prominent results panel may draw the eye before the method. Bar heights appear consistent with the checklist at the available resolution, which does not support checking exact values from the bars alone. This assessment is an AI review.
